newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close higher amid quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close higher amid quiet trade.

text.p: Argentine stocks closed 0.66 percent higher Friday, putting the advance for the week at 0.64 percent, amid quiet market conditions and little activity, traders said.
"The market was very calm, with few trades, but we had expected a market correction today," said Gabriel Armando, an analyst at Galicia Valores.
"The economy is showing strong indications of a rebound and the expectations are that the rebound will pick up," he added.
The leading blue-chip Merval .MERV stock index rose 0.66 percent to 607.06, while the bolsa's general index rose 0.50 percent.
Sixty-two stocks were traded this session with 30 rising, 16 falling and 16 unchanged amid trade volume of 19.5 million pesos compared with 23 million pesos on Thursday.
Among market leaders the biggest gainers were builder Polledo that put in a rise of 5.05 percent and steel-maker Acindar that rose 3.78 percent.
In the coming week, traders expect the market to consolidate after a series of consecutive gains.
Market players point out that the Merval has a clear resistance level at 610 index points, a point it was unable to breach in the recent sessions.
According to traders, at the end of next week there could be a pick-up in liquidity with the arrival of new cash from overseas by investment funds that closed positions this week.
Separately, brokerage house Bonival sold a seat on the stock exchange to Mercurio brokerage for $600,000.
